39. CULTIV ATION OF VEGETABLES IN NET 
HOUSE/POLYNET HOUSE
1. CApsICum
Capsicum can be cultivated in 3.0 and 6.5 m height polynet 
house and naturally ventilated polyhouse with following method:
Selection of Hybrid : Green colored Capsicum hybrids

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
“Bharat and Indra” are recommended for cultivation under both 
nethouse/polynethouse and naturally ventilated poly-houses. 
Yellow colored “Orobelle” and red colored “Bomby” Capsicum 
hybrids are recommended for cultivation under naturally ventilated 
poly-houses only.
Based on the method of irrigation, cultivation of Capsicum 
in net-house/polynet-house and naturally ventilated poly-house is 
given as under :
(A)  Capsicum crop under drip irrigation

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
Seed rate and nursery raising – For an area of 1 acre, 12,000 
seedlings are required. Sow capsicum nursery in the first week of 
August in pro-trays. Treat the seed with 3g of Captan per kg of 
seed before sowing. Before transplanting, drench pro-trays with 
Bavistin @ 2g/l of water. 
Land preparation and fertilizer application : Add 80 tonnes 
of well-decomposed farmyard manure per acre in the first year 
and 20 tonnes per acre in the subsequent years. Add DAP @ 100

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
kg and CaNO3 @ 25 kg per acre every year and then prepare the 
land to a fine tilth.
Bed Size : Mark the plot in nethouse/polynethouse and 
naturally ventilated poly-houses with rope at 1.5 m spacing, 
leaving at least 30 cm (1 foot) from all side walls. Then make beds 
of 1m width and 15 cm (1/2 foot) height with 50 cm row/path and 
slant from center of bed to both sides, rather than flat bed.
Transplanting : Use 35-40 days old seedlings for transplanting

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
in 2nd-3rd week of September. Transplant in early morning/ late 
evening.Plant at shallow depth of 2-2.5 cm. (In case of absence 
of provision for polysheet on the roof of net-houses in rains and 
shade-net in both net-house/poly-house in summer, sowing and 
134 135
transplanting can be delayed but it will have direct effect on the 
yield of capsicum)
Spacing : Seedlings should be transplanted in a paired row 
pattern with row to row and plant to plant @ 45 cm ×45 cm (1.5

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
×1.5 foot) from the centre of bed, with zigzag transplanting i.e. 
in a triangle shape (means plants of second row should be placed 
in the centre and parallel of the plants of the first row) and the 
spacing between the paired rows should be 105 cm.
Irrigation : If possible, it is advisable to install the drip 
irrigation system in the net-/poly-house. One  lateral per bed with 
drippers spaced at 30 cm having discharge of 2.25 l/hr should

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
be used. Water the beds to field capacity up-to 15 days after 
transplanting and then operate drip daily as per the timings given 
below:

Production Measures 
Pruning and number of branches : Do pinching after 5-6 
pairs of leaves. It will give 5-6 branches after few days. Select 4

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
best branches, preferably in opposite direction. Remove all flowers 
for 1 month. Remove side shoots at weekly interval. Pruning starts 
15-20 days after transplanting. Two steel strings per bed should be 
overhung at the gutter level of net-/poly-house, running parallel 
alongside the length of the bed.Twining (tying) of 4 branches 
136 137
should be done 30 days after transplanting with blue or green 
colored plastic twines, not gunny threads. Two branches of a plant

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
should be tied to one steel string and the other two branches of a 
plant to the other string running parallel overhead. This will open 
up the plant and help in ventilation. 
Removal of lower older leaves : As the plants grow up and 
fruit is harvested, remove lower and older leaves at least 1 feet or 
more from the ground. 
Micronutrient and Growth regulator foliar sprays 
(Under 6.5 m structure height) : Give foliar spray of Microsol 
B (micronutrient) @ 0.5 g/l water + Spic Cytozyme (growth

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
regulator) @ 2 ml/l water at fortnightly intervals after transplanting. 
Spray growth regulators Lihocin/ Cycocel (chlormequat chloride) 
@ 300 ppm (3g/l of water) + NAA (Planofix) @ 25 ppm (0.25g/l 
of water) 2.5 months after transplanting, along with Microsol and 
Spic Cytozyme, at fornightly interval.
But under 3 m structure height,  start spraying Lihocin/ 
Cycocel along with Microsol and Spic Cytozyme, while spray of 
NAA should be started 2.5 months after transplanting.

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
Shade net : Use 50% white or red colored shade net placed 
at gutter level from September to mid-October and then April 
onwards till the end to protect the crop during hot months. Putting 
shade net over the rooffrom outside will give less reduction in 
heat. 
Ventilators opening/ closing : In winter, all ventilators of 
poly-house should be closed at night to obtain maximum yield. 
Always open ventilators for at least 2-3 hours each day even in 
severe winters for exchange of air.

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
(* Net-house should have provision of poly-sheet during rains 
and winter months. During summer, provide roof-top ventilation 
in case of polynet-house. Roof should not be fully closed with 
poly-sheet)
Harvesting : >60 g green colored fruits and >100 g yellow 
and red colored fruits are preferred in the market. In case of 
September transplanted crop, the green colored fruits are ready 
for harvest in mid-November and yellow and red colored fruits 
136 137

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
in mid-Dec ember. September transplanted crop gives 11 and 
31 percent more and early yield advantage over October and 
November transplanted crop, respectively.
Yield : Yield of capsicum hybrids depend on the height of 
protected structure, time of transplanting, type of irrigation system 
and use of shade-net and poly-sheet.
September transplanted green colored Indra gives yield of 580 
and 443 q/acre under 6.5m and 3m structure height, respectively,

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
while Orobelle (yellow colored) give yield of 315 and 162 q/acre 
and Bomby (red colored)  give yield of 322 and 167 q/acre under 
6.5m and 3m structure height, respectively. 
(B) Capsicum crop under furrow irrigation 
Sowing and  transplanting time should be as given under 
drip irrigation. Seedlings should be transplanted on 15 cm high 
raised beds with a spacing  of  90 cm ×30 cm, accommodating 
15,000 plants/acre. The fertilizer should be applied as per the

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
recommendation mentioned in the package of practices for 
open field cultivation  of capsicum. Cover the beds with a black 
polythene mulch of 25 micron thickness. Mulching increases early 
and total fruit yield, extends shelf life of fruits and improves fruit 
quality, especially colour of the fruits. The mulched crop produces 
maximum early and total fruit yield when seed is sown around 
Ist of October and seedlings are transplanted about a month later.

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
Yield of November transplanted Bharat and Indra is 225 and 255 
q/acre respectively, when white/red colored shade net is used from 
April onwards and 160  and 180 q/acre respectively without the  
use of shade net. If the net-house has the provision of both poly-
sheet and shade-net, then September transplanted Indra gives 
yield of  310 q/acre.
2. Tomato
(A) Cultivation of Tomato in Net house
The Cultivation of tomato varieties, Punjab Swarna, Punjab

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
Gaurav, Punjab Sartaj, Punjab Sona Cherry, Punjab Red Cherry 
and Punjab Kesar Cherry are recommended in net house and poly 
house cultivation.
Only indeterminate varieties/hybrids by virtue of their having 
long fruiting span can be  grown successfully in net-house where 
138 139
fruit maturity is advanced by 20-25 days as compared to open field 
conditions. Cover the beds with a black polythene mulch of 25 
micron thickness. Mulching increases early and total fruit yield,

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
extends shelf life of fruits and improves fruit quality especially 
colour of the fruits. The mulched crop produces maximum early 
and total fruit yield when seed is sown around 25 th of September 
and seedlings are transplanted about a month later. Seedlings 
should be transplanted on 15 cm high raised beds keeping a 
spacing of 1.25 m ×30 cm. Plants should be trained upright with 
the support of bamboos with nylon ropes. All cultural practices

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
should be followed as mentioned in the package of practices for 
open field cultivation of tomato crop.
(B) Cultivation of Tomato in Naturally Ventilated Poly 
house
Seed rate and nursery raising : For an area of 100 m 2, 1.5 
g of seed is sufficient. Sow tomato nursery in the last week of 
September, which will be ready for transplanting in 25-30 days 
after sowing. Treat the seed with 3g Captan or Thiram per kg of 
seed before sowing. Nursery should be raised in the same polynet-

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
house in which crop is to be grown to protect the seedling from 
white fly, a vector for viruses and other insect- pests.
Land preparation and fertilizer application : Prepare the 
land to a fine tilth and apply well-decomposed farmyard manure 
@ 2.5 q/100 m 2 15 days before transplanting. Apply urea 3.0 
kg/100 m2 in 4 equal splits (1/4, 3-4 days prior to transplanting, 
1/4, 25 days after transplanting, 1/4, 45 days after transplanting

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
and the remaining 1/4, 90 days after transplanting). For P and K, 
apply Single Super phosphate 4.0 kg/100 m 2 and 1.1 kg Muriate 
of Potash/100 m2 as basal dose with first split dose of urea. If the 
crop is drip irrigated, than apply 3.0kg/100 m2 of urea in 15 equal 
splits at 10 days interval along with irrigation.
Spacing : To utilize the space efficiently, seedlings should be 
transplanted in the polynet-house in a paired rows pattern with

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
plant-to-plant spacing of 30 cm. The spacing between two paired 
rows should be 90 cm and row-to-row spacing within the paired 
line should be 60 cm.
138 139
Irrigation : If possible., it is advisable to install the drip 
irrigation system in the polynet-house as it reduces the humidity 
build up and weed problem. First irrigation for surface irrigation 
is to be given just after transplanting. Initially for a few days, 
regular irrigation is to be applied for the establishment of the crop.

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
Subsequent irrigation should be applied at 4 to 5 days interval 
depending upon the soil and climatic conditions. If the crop is 
drip irrigated then irrigation should be applied at 4-5 days interval 
in the month of November-February, 2-3 days interval in the 
month of March and 1-2 days interval in the month of April-May 
depending upon the climatic conditions. Application of urea along 
with irrigation (fertigation) helps in saving the quantity of fertilizer

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
and labour besides improving the yield and quality of produce. 
The drip irrigation results in 48% saving of water as compared to 
surface irrigation. Don’t allow the plants to wilt at any time. Fruit 
will be damaged if the plants do not get appropriate amount of 
water and fertilizer regularly.
Earthing up and pruning : After 20-25 days of transplanting, 
earthing up is to be done. Prune the plants in a polynet-house to 
a single stem for better growth of fruits. All lateral branches must

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
be removed when they are one to three inches long. This allows 
for maximum air circulation and reduces pest control problems. 
Pruning must be done regularly and plants should be checked at 
least once a week. Because of indeterminate nature of polynet-
house tomato, the crop should be staked properly to get higher 
yields. The staking method involves the use of wooden stakes 
placed within the row of plants and running a number of parallel

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
pieces of string or wire from stake to stake and trapping the new 
growth of plant between the strings. This keeps the plants in an 
upright position preventing the fruit from touching the ground.
Harvesting : The fruits will be ready for harvesting in the 
last week of February, which will continue up to first fortnight of 
May. The average yield under naturally ventilated polynet-house 
condition is about 264 q/acre with surface irrigation and about 384

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
q/acre with drip irrigation and fertigation.
140 141
(C) Cultivation of Tomato in soilless media  
Tomato hybirds, NS-4266, Himshekhar and Punjab Sartaj 
can be grown in soilless medium under naturally ventilated 
polyhouse.
3. Cultivation of Cucumber in soilless media under  
naturally ventilated polyhouse
Selection of Cultivar 
Parthenocarpic cucumber cultivars like hybrid Multistar or 
Kafka and PAU variety Punjab Kheera 1 are recommended for

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
growing under naturally ventilated polyhouse /poly net house.
Seed rate and nursery raising
For an area of 500 m 2, 1500 seeds (15 g) are sufficient. Sow, 
the cucumber seed in mid of September and it will be ready for 
transplanting in 15-20 days after sowing. Transplant the nursery in 
first week of October. The second crop can be taken by sowing the 
nursery in January, which will become ready for transplanting in 
30-35 days after sowing. Transplant the nursery in first fortnight

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
of February. The nursery raising is done in trays, each having 50 
conical shaped cells (Plate-1a). The cells are filled with coco-peat 
saturated with nutrient solution. Before the placement of the seed 
in growing media in the cells, impressions of 1.0-1.5 cm deep 
are made. One seed per cell is placed in horizontal position at 
1.0-1.5 cm depth from the surface. After placing the seed in all 
the cells, the seed is covered with more growing media and the

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
excess was removed by striking off a ruler. During nursery stages 
the seedlings should also be fed with nutrient solution for getting 
healthy nursery/seedlings. 
Seed Bed Preparation while shifting from soil to soilless 
media cultivation: 
Shifting from soil cultivation to soilless (coco peat) media 
based cultivation involves the following steps. The first step 
involves levelling the greenhouse with a proper slope. A -slope 
of 1-1.5 % is provided to soil in polyhouse from north to south

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
direction for the collection of the leachate. The entire surface 
area of the greenhouse floor should be covered with weed mat for 
140 141
avoidance of weed emergence and to eliminate contact between 
soil and growing media. 
Plastic troughs, each of thickness 500 μ and dimensions of 
20.0 m length × 0.60 m width are laid on the weed mat at 90 
cm between two adjacent troughs. The spacing trays each having 
dimensions of 50.0 cm × 60 cm are laid on the plastic troughs to

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
facilitate drainage of leachate. The next step is the placement of 
coco-peat slabs and the installation of subsequent drip lines for 
the supply of nutrient solution to the plants. Once the system is 
operated, there would be a need for a collection unit for collecting 
the drained leachate from the system. Therefore, setting of the 
leachate unit is a pre-requisite for soilless cultivation. 
Setting up of fertigation system 
The crop should be supplied with fertigation of single strength

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
solution in plastic tank of 1000 litre capacity containing all macro 
and micro nutrients. All macro and micro nutrients are weighed 
in required quantity and mixed in one packet and dissolved in 4-5 
litres water in a bucket and dissolved and filtered by passing through 
a muslin cloth. Filtered solution is put into 1000 litre of water in 
fertigation tank. The desired EC is 2.0 –3.0 dS/m and pH between 
5.8-6.5 should be kept. Acidification is done using phosphoric

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
acid to adjust pH of the fertigation solution. For example 0.26 ml 
phosphoric acid (85 %) per 1 liter of nutrient solution is added 
to lower pH from 7.2 to 6.2. The prepared nutrient solution was 
monitored on regular basis for EC and pH value. The frequency of 
fertigation varies from 3-5 times per day, however duration (4-13 
minute) of fertigation is governed by the crop growth stage and 
prevailing weather conditions. 
The main components include a filter, pressure gauge and

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
timers. For preventing the clogging of emitters, the nutrient 
solution from the tank is passed through filter before its delivery 
to the plant root system. The system include timer for operating 
the fertigation automatically.  The time to operate the fertigation 
system is set in the timer for a pre-determined time. The timers 
allowed the application of nutrient solution for a pre-determined 
time and stopped automatically after the completion of pre-set

chunks.title: pp veg
chunks.text:
time. To deliver the nutrient solution safely and at desired rate 
142 143
to the root zone of the plants, the operating pressure of emitters 
is regulated using pressure gauge. The system is operated at a 
pressure of 1.5 kg/cm2.

4. Transplantation 
On each coco-peat slab, three square holes of   are cut, keeping 
a 30.0 cm spacing between any two adjacent holes. The slabs are 
kept under saturation for at least 24 hour before transplanting. The 
seedlings become ready for planting after attaining 3-4 true leaf 
stage. The seedlings planted with 3-4 true leaves, give first picking 
about 30 days after transplanting.
